title: Incident & Postmortem
description: Vocabulario de on-call, gestión de incidents en tiempo real y postmortems blameless: roles (IC, scribe, comms), mitigation vs remediation, blast radius, cascading failures y acciones de recovery.

vocab.example: I got paged at 4am for elevated 5xx on the checkout service.
Spinning up a war room in Zoom — link in #incidents.

vocab.translation: líder de la respuesta al incidente
vocab.example: Sara is the incident commander for this one — direct all updates through her.
I'll IC this incident — someone else take scribe.
Can someone volunteer as scribe? We need the timeline for the postmortem.
I've got comms — I'll post updates to the status page every 15 minutes.
Mitigation is in place — traffic is now routed to the healthy region.
Mitigated for now; full remediation will land in tomorrow's deploy.
The root cause was a misconfigured retry policy amplifying load.
The lack of a circuit breaker was a contributing factor, not the root cause.
Blast radius is limited to EU users on iOS — roughly 3% of traffic.
Reminder: this postmortem is blameless — focus on systems, not individuals.
Action item: add alerting on queue depth by end of next week.
Filed three follow-ups in Jira — linked at the bottom of the doc.
We caught the bug because the on-call engineer was dogfooding the mobile app.
Would a gradual rollout have caught this earlier? Yes — one percent to start.
Rolling back to v247 — ETA two minutes.
Deploy freeze is in effect until we finish the postmortem.

vocab.translation: botón de emergencia para apagar algo
vocab.example: We hit the red button and disabled the new checkout flow entirely.
Good news: there's a kill switch — flipping it now.
The cache expired and we got a thundering herd on the database.
One service timing out triggered a cascading failure across five downstream systems.
We're in a brownout — logged-in users are fine, but signups are failing.
Search is degraded — results are slow but returning.

vocab.translation: tasa de errores por encima de lo normal
vocab.example: We're seeing elevated 5xx from the payment gateway — starting investigation.
CPU is at saturation on the primary — scaling out now.

vocab.translation: presión hacia atrás en el sistema
vocab.example: The consumer is applying backpressure — producers are slowing down as expected.
The queue backlog is 40k messages and climbing.
Draining traffic from the unhealthy node before restart.
Quarantined the flaky worker so it stops processing new jobs.
The bulkhead pattern saved us — the failure didn't spread to other tenants.
The synthetic monitor was the canary in the coal mine — it fired 20 minutes before real users noticed.

vocab.translation: prueba rápida de que todo funciona
vocab.example: Running a smoke test post-rollback to confirm the site is healthy.
The load balancer stopped routing to the pod once the healthcheck failed three times.
The outage was caused by a third-party dependency we don't control.
The upstream service is sending malformed payloads.
We need to notify the downstream teams before we take this offline.

vocab.translation: pico repentino de tráfico o métrica
vocab.example: There was a huge spike in requests right after the marketing email went out.
Median latency looks fine, but tail latency is awful — p99 is 4 seconds.
Our p99 blew past the SLO by an order of magnitude.
First few requests are slow due to cold start — expected after a scale-out.
We warm up the caches before shifting traffic to the new region.
Give it a minute for the cache to hydrate before you start load testing.
We restored from the last snapshot taken 15 minutes before the incident.

vocab.translation: aplicado hacia atrás en el tiempo
vocab.example: We can't apply the fix retroactively — the corrupt data needs a manual backfill.

vocab.translation: cobertura on-call en múltiples zonas horarias
vocab.example: We run a follow-the-sun rotation across EMEA, Americas and APAC.
Handoff notes are in the runbook doc — nothing on fire right now.

vocab.translation: guía paso a paso para operar
vocab.example: Following the runbook — step 3 is to failover to the standby.
Declaring this a SEV1 — full customer impact on payments.

vocab.translation: señal de que el incidente terminó
vocab.example: Metrics are back to baseline — calling the all-clear at 14:32 UTC.

listening.text: We're seeing elevated 5xx from the checkout service starting around 14:03 UTC.
IC me — I'll take comms as well until someone else jumps in.
Rolling back to version 42, ETA about five minutes. Please hold off on any deploys.
Blast radius is limited to European users on the mobile app — desktop is unaffected.
The mitigation is in place, but we still need to figure out the root cause before we can close this out.
Deploy freeze is in effect until further notice — reach out to the release manager if you need an exception.
Metrics have been back to baseline for fifteen minutes — I'm calling the all-clear.
Reminder that this postmortem is blameless. We're focused on systems and process, not people.
The queue backlog is at forty thousand messages and climbing — we need to scale the consumers now.
Handoff notes are in the runbook. Nothing on fire — the P2 from yesterday is mitigated.

speaking.target: The trigger was a config change at 13:58, but the underlying cause was a missing validation that let an invalid value reach production.
We identified three action items: add schema validation on config, alert on error rate deviations, and document the rollback procedure.
This was not caused by human error — the system failed to prevent a foreseeable mistake, and that's what we need to fix.
The blast radius was smaller than it could have been thanks to the gradual rollout — we caught it at the two percent stage.
Time to detection was fast at four minutes, but time to mitigation was almost an hour — that's our biggest gap.
Post the first update to a #incidents channel: elevated errors on payments, IC assigned, investigation starting.
Give a two-minute verbal summary of a SEV1 to leadership: what happened, impact, current status, ETA to resolution.
Open a blameless postmortem: state the scope, the timeline in one sentence, and set expectations for the discussion.
